query: For high-entropy-alloy protective coatings in wear-resistant applications, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs their wear performance and why? Define a controlled change that would distinguish the hypothesis from a baseline, the directional observations expected if it is correct, the range over which it should hold, the prior evidence that supports it, and an observation that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: The wear resistance of high-entropy‐alloy (HEA) protective coatings is governed by the in‐situ formation of a continuous, hard, alumina‐rich tribofilm whose thickness scales with the Al content in the alloy.
generation.material_initial_state: Magnetron‐sputtered CoCrFeNi HEA coatings with systematically varied Al contents (0, 5, 10, 15 at.%).
generation.intervention: Increase Al concentration from 0 to 15 at.% in the CoCrFeNi base HEA composition.
generation.conditions: Pin‐on‐disk sliding against a hardened steel ball, 5 N normal load, 0.1 m/s sliding speed, ambient laboratory air (≈25 °C, 50 % RH), 1000 m total sliding distance.
generation.structural_mediator: Thickness and continuity of the tribologically generated Al‐rich oxide layer on the wear track.
generation.mechanism: Al atoms preferentially oxidize under sliding contact to form a protective alumina‐rich tribofilm that reduces adhesive and abrasive material removal.
generation.predicted_outcome: With each 5 at.% increase in Al content, the tribofilm thickness will increase by ≈100 nm and the specific wear rate will decrease by ≈20 % relative to the Al‐free baseline.
generation.baseline: Wear rate and oxide‐film thickness measured on the CoCrFeNi coating with 0 at.% Al under identical test conditions.
generation.boundary: Holds for Al contents between 5–20 at.% and sliding loads up to 10 N at room temperature in humid air; not expected to apply under vacuum or inert‐gas environments where oxide formation is suppressed.
generation.uncertainty: Medium; while Al is known to form protective oxides, the exact thickness‐to‐wear reduction scaling may vary with interactions among Co, Cr, Fe, Ni and test parameters.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare three coatings (0, 10, 15 at.% Al). Perform pin‐on‐disk tests as above. After testing, measure wear volume and map oxide thickness/composition across the wear track using cross‐sectional SEM and XPS depth profiling.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If increasing Al content does not produce a thicker alumina‐rich tribofilm or if wear rate does not decrease commensurately (no clear positive correlation between film thickness and wear reduction), the hypothesis is falsified.
